description: Provisional editorial subject summaries based on the indicated representative public comment. These explain form-letter content; they are not theme predictions, verified authorship, or evidence of coordinated submissions.

CDC-2026-1387-0042.subject: Retain disability questions and health-policy data
CDC-2026-1387-0042.summary: Urges CDC to keep detailed disability measures so disability-related health needs, access barriers, and policy outcomes remain measurable.

CDC-2026-1387-0401.subject: Restore ME/CFS, Long COVID, fatigue, and PEM measures
CDC-2026-1387-0401.summary: Requests questions on ME/CFS, Long COVID, fatigue, and post-exertional malaise, while retaining proposed-to-be-removed disability items.

CDC-2026-1387-1092.subject: Restore ME/CFS tracking, fatigue, and disability measures
CDC-2026-1387-1092.summary: Opposes omission of ME/CFS and asks to restore fatigue and post-exertional malaise questions and preserve disability metrics.

CDC-2026-1387-0412.subject: Reuse established ME/CFS and Long COVID questions
CDC-2026-1387-0412.summary: Requests previously used ME/CFS diagnosis and current-status questions and established Long COVID duration and current-symptom questions.

CDC-2026-1387-1608.subject: Keep intellectual disability and mental-health measures
CDC-2026-1387-1608.summary: Opposes cuts to detailed intellectual disability, communication, and mental-health measures used to monitor services and rights.

CDC-2026-1387-0580.subject: Preserve ME/CFS and Long COVID representation
CDC-2026-1387-0580.summary: Calls for ME/CFS, Long COVID, fatigue, post-exertional malaise, and disability questions, citing the impact of severe chronic illness.

CDC-2026-1387-0299.subject: Restore developmental-disability identification questions
CDC-2026-1387-0299.summary: Questions why three adult-survey items used to identify developmental disabilities are missing from the proposed design.

CDC-2026-1387-0028.subject: Disability question cuts and accessible survey participation
CDC-2026-1387-0028.summary: Raises concerns about reduced disability measures and whether changes in survey administration will exclude people with disabilities.

CDC-2026-1387-0318.subject: Retain identification of intellectual and developmental disabilities
CDC-2026-1387-0318.summary: Requests continued identification of people with intellectual and developmental disabilities, including autism and related needs.

CDC-2026-1387-0333.subject: Collect detailed disability and mental-health diagnoses
CDC-2026-1387-0333.summary: Advocates disability-type-specific statistics, including neurodevelopmental and psychosocial conditions, for health monitoring.

CDC-2026-1387-0491.subject: Add ME/CFS and Long COVID questions and a 2027–28 crosswalk
CDC-2026-1387-0491.summary: Recommends specific chronic-condition, fatigue, and disability items, continued sponsored content, and a public item crosswalk.

CDC-2026-1387-0569.subject: Count severe ME/CFS and related functional limitations
CDC-2026-1387-0569.summary: Requests measures for ME/CFS, fatigue, and disability so severe illness and functional limitations remain visible in national statistics.

CDC-2026-1387-1134.subject: Track ME/CFS and Long COVID, including PEM
CDC-2026-1387-1134.summary: Opposes eliminating ME/CFS and Long COVID monitoring and urges retention of fatigue, post-exertional malaise, and disability measures.

CDC-2026-1387-0014.subject: Measure caregiver assistance and environmental supports
CDC-2026-1387-0014.summary: Supports shorter, accessible response options while requesting measures of caregiving, assistive technology, and home conditions affecting functioning.

CDC-2026-1387-0026.subject: Preserve disability questions and accessible participation
CDC-2026-1387-0026.summary: Calls for disability and developmental-disability questions and raises equity, internet-access, and in-person follow-up concerns.

CDC-2026-1387-0034.subject: Protect survey content, trend comparability, and review process
CDC-2026-1387-0034.summary: Warns that reducing questionnaire scope and changing modes may weaken trend monitoring; suggests delaying changes and expert review.

CDC-2026-1387-0111.subject: Retain disability and accessible health-care measures
CDC-2026-1387-0111.summary: Urges retention of disability-related questions that document care barriers, treatment needs, and health experiences of people with disabilities.

CDC-2026-1387-0141.subject: Retain detailed disability and health-access questions
CDC-2026-1387-0141.summary: Argues that proposed disability question removals would reduce information needed to identify disparities and unmet health-care needs.

CDC-2026-1387-0163.subject: Keep detailed functioning and Washington Group measures
CDC-2026-1387-0163.summary: Opposes cuts to upper-body function, fatigue, hearing, mobility, and psychosocial functioning; asks about testing and consultation.

CDC-2026-1387-0204.subject: Measure Deaf and DeafBlind communication access
CDC-2026-1387-0204.summary: Requests questions about Deaf, DeafBlind, and hard-of-hearing health needs and communication accommodations such as ASL and captioning.

CDC-2026-1387-0282.subject: Measure disability supports and refugee access barriers
CDC-2026-1387-0282.summary: Requests developmental-disability and support-needs measures plus accessible multilingual survey participation for refugees and immigrants with disabilities.

CDC-2026-1387-0308.subject: Include a wider range of diseases and disabilities
CDC-2026-1387-0308.summary: Lists physical, mental, developmental, and chronic conditions for continued measurement of prevalence and health-care access.

CDC-2026-1387-0425.subject: Retain disability questions and interviewer assistance
CDC-2026-1387-0425.summary: Opposes reducing disability measures and replacing interviewer-supported modes with less accessible administration methods.

CDC-2026-1387-0446.subject: Restore post-infection illness questions
CDC-2026-1387-0446.summary: Requests recognition of Long COVID, ME/CFS, and related post-infection conditions to support diagnosis and public-health monitoring.

CDC-2026-1387-0504.subject: Track ME/CFS and Long COVID with fatigue and PEM
CDC-2026-1387-0504.summary: Calls for ME/CFS, Long COVID, fatigue, post-exertional malaise, and disability questions using lived-experience examples.

CDC-2026-1387-0737.subject: Assess internet-mode bias, response rates, and burden
CDC-2026-1387-0737.summary: Questions self-administered web-survey response rates, nonresponse bias, representativeness, and questionnaire length.

CDC-2026-1387-1137.subject: Restore chronic-illness, fatigue, and disability tracking
CDC-2026-1387-1137.summary: Requests ME/CFS and Long COVID monitoring, post-exertional malaise and fatigue measures, and preservation of disability metrics.

CDC-2026-1387-1182.subject: Retain Long COVID, ME/CFS, fatigue, and disability questions
CDC-2026-1387-1182.summary: A family account urges tracking Long COVID and ME/CFS, post-exertional malaise, fatigue, and disability in the redesigned survey.

CDC-2026-1387-1409.subject: Preserve chronic-illness measures and comparable trends
CDC-2026-1387-1409.summary: Opposes removing Long COVID, ME/CFS, and disability items and emphasizes continuity, research, and survey quality.
